mission: Own schedules and occurrences while routing effects through Codex and the operation ledger.
runtimeTopology: The existing AutomationStore remains the durable definition/run owner and scheduler. The fenced executor consumes one occurrence claim and routes typed effects through an injected effect driver.
physicalState: Definitions, runs and event chains are SQLite-backed and generation-fenced. Executor receipts bind occurrence, step, operation, semantic digest, final payload and terminality; downstream domain facts stay outside TaskFlow.
linearization: Definition registration and scheduler tick use owner transactions. Claims advance a monotone fence. Step dispatch occurs only after dependency success and final-payload equality.
recovery: Unknown effects block dependent steps. Compensation is a separate authorized step. Event-chain corruption, stale fences, expired claims and changed operation semantics reject.
security: TaskFlow cannot mint final-use authority or call providers/Matrix/browser directly. Capability sets, graph acyclicity, recovery paths and immutable operation identities are validated.
capacity: Occurrences <=1024 per bounded scan, nodes <=256, edges <=1024, executor steps <=128. Catch-up, retries and ready steps are bounded by policy.
terminalObserver: The downstream effect adapter is the terminal observer. TaskFlow records terminal or indeterminate receipts and never infers success from queue admission.
externalEvidenceGaps: deployed App Server/effect adapter callsite and trusted external terminal observer
target scheduler timezone database, DST, crash-reopen and compensation qualification
